questiontext.text:
The [[if test="is(f=\"rx\")"]]reflection in the x-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(f=\"ry\")"]]reflection in the y-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(f=\"ryx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(f=\"rmyx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = -x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(f=\"r90\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise about O[[/if]][[if test="is(f=\"r180\")"]]rotation of \(180^\circ\) about O[[/if]][[if test="is(f=\"r270\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) clockwise about O[[/if]] is followed by the [[if test="is(s=\"rx\")"]]reflection in the x-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(s=\"ry\")"]]reflection in the y-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(s=\"ryx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(s=\"rmyx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = -x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(s=\"r90\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise about O[[/if]][[if test="is(s=\"r180\")"]]rotation of \(180^\circ\) about O[[/if]][[if test="is(s=\"r270\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) clockwise about O[[/if]].

(a) Write down the single matrix for the combined transformation.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Which single transformation is it?

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
The matrix of the [[if test="is(f=\"rx\")"]]reflection in the x-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(f=\"ry\")"]]reflection in the y-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(f=\"ryx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(f=\"rmyx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = -x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(f=\"r90\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise about O[[/if]][[if test="is(f=\"r180\")"]]rotation of \(180^\circ\) about O[[/if]][[if test="is(f=\"r270\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) clockwise about O[[/if]] is \({@Fm@}\) and the matrix of the [[if test="is(s=\"rx\")"]]reflection in the x-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(s=\"ry\")"]]reflection in the y-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(s=\"ryx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(s=\"rmyx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = -x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(s=\"r90\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise about O[[/if]][[if test="is(s=\"r180\")"]]rotation of \(180^\circ\) about O[[/if]][[if test="is(s=\"r270\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) clockwise about O[[/if]] is \({@Sm@}\). The first transformation's matrix goes on the right:

\({@Sm@}{@Fm@} = {@ta@}\)

(b) Read its columns: (1, 0) goes to \(({@ta[1,1]@},\,{@ta[2,1]@})\) and (0, 1) goes to \(({@ta[1,2]@},\,{@ta[2,2]@})\). This is the [[if test="is(rk=\"rx\")"]]reflection in the x-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(rk=\"ry\")"]]reflection in the y-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(rk=\"ryx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(rk=\"rmyx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = -x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(rk=\"r90\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise about O[[/if]][[if test="is(rk=\"r180\")"]]rotation of \(180^\circ\) about O[[/if]][[if test="is(rk=\"r270\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) clockwise about O[[/if]].

questiondescription.text:
Matrices and Transformations: one transformation equal to two

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.1: Find the single matrix for one reflection or rotation followed by another, and name the single transformation.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 13, Exercise F, Question 1 of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 5 (Metric), ed. P. G. Bowie, Cambridge University Press, 1969: combinations given by name and worked with matrices instead of drawings, the result named from a list, randomised.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: That is the matrix for the other order. The first transformation's matrix goes on the right: (second) \(\times\) (first).

feedbackvariables.text: cm2: if ans2="id" then matrix([1,0],[0,1]) else sm(ans2);

truefeedback.text: That is the result of doing them in the other order.
